sri_lanka.title: 'Poison seller' Kenneth Law apologises in court to the families of his victims

cards.what_happened: Kenneth Law, a 61-year-old Canadian former chef who sold toxic chemicals through online suicide forums in 40 countries, apologised in court on Friday to the families of his victims. He spoke at a sentencing hearing in an Ontario court, where prosecutors asked for 25 years in prison and his defence lawyer asked for 12. He pleaded guilty in May to 14 counts of aiding the suicide deaths of 14 people in Ontario and has admitted causing the deaths of dozens of victims in England and Wales.
details: Kenneth Law, a 61-year-old former chef from Canada, sold toxic chemicals to people he met in online suicide forums, sending about 1,200 packages to recipients in 40 countries, with roughly a quarter of them going to the UK. On Friday he spoke at his sentencing hearing in an Ontario court, telling the families of victims that he deeply regrets his actions and will never repeat them. He said words can never replace the loss of their loved ones, offered his deepest condolences, and said he remains remorseful and sorry.

Law pleaded guilty in May to 14 counts of aiding the suicide deaths of 14 people in Ontario, Canada. He has also admitted causing the deaths of dozens of victims in England and Wales. Under a plea deal, Canadian authorities withdrew more serious charges of murder, and he will not face charges in the UK or over any British deaths.

At Friday's hearing, prosecutors asked the judge for a 25-year prison term and stressed that many victims were young and struggling with mental distress. Because he would get credit for time served since his May 2023 arrest, the recommended sentence would mean just under 20 years in prison. Crown Attorney Kathleen Doherty called Law a predator who took advantage of vulnerable people, saying they needed help but found Law and his products for death, and she said his motive was financial: if people could pay, he sold to them, with no questions about their circumstances.

Defence lawyer Matthew Gourlay disagreed, arguing Law was not responsible for the victims' battles with mental illness, that each incident is its own unique tragedy, and that while Law may be a common denominator, he was not the cause of the hardships that made people seek his products; Gourlay said Law held a misguided belief that he was helping, and asked for a 12-year sentence. The hearing followed an emotional few days of testimony in September, when grieving family members and friends told the court about the pain Law caused. Those impact statements will be taken into account at sentencing, which is due at a later date, and the BBC pointed readers to its Action Line for organisations that offer information to anyone affected.
key_facts: Kenneth Law, 61, a Canadian former chef, sold toxic chemicals through online suicide forums.
About 1,200 packages went to 40 countries; roughly a quarter were sent to the UK.
He pleaded guilty in May to 14 counts over 14 suicide deaths in Ontario.
He admitted dozens of deaths in England and Wales; murder charges were withdrawn under a plea deal.
Under the plea deal he faces no UK charges over British deaths.
Prosecutors want 25 years, defence wants 12; time served since May 2023 arrest counts.
Doherty called him a predator; Gourlay said he had a misguided belief he helped.
Sentencing is due later, after September family impact statements are considered.
cards.whats_next: Sentencing is due at a later date, and the impact statements from grieving family members and friends given in September will be taken into account.

cards.what_happened: Two Sri Lankan migrant workers died in a road accident in Hwaseong, South Korea, at around 9 p.m. on Nov. 26, 2026. The Sri Lankan Embassy in Seoul was informed by Korean police on Nov. 27. Sri Lanka’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism is coordinating with South Korean authorities and the families to repatriate the remains, Acting Minister Arun Hemachandra said.
details: Acting Minister of Foreign Affairs Arun Hemachandra said the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Foreign Employment and Tourism is working with South Korean authorities and the families of the two Sri Lankan migrant workers. The aim is to facilitate the return of their remains after the road accident in Hwaseong, South Korea.
The accident happened at around 9 p.m. on Nov. 26, 2026. The Sri Lankan Embassy in Seoul was officially told by Korean police on Nov. 27.

The Embassy’s Consular Section is coordinating the required formalities with relevant authorities, the ministry and the families. It is doing this to speed up the repatriation process and to give consular and welfare assistance.
Hemachandra said both workers had gone to South Korea after registering with the Sri Lanka Bureau of Foreign Employment (SLBFE).

cards.what_happened: A man is suspected of killing a 45-year-old woman. Police say a financial dispute led him to attack her with a sharp weapon. He fled, hit a wild elephant, and was hospitalised.
details: The source is a newswire. A man is suspected of killing a 45-year-old woman in the Mahailluppallama area of Eppawala. He was hospitalised after he hit a wild elephant while he was running away.

Police said the killing happened in the early hours of Friday (27). It followed a financial dispute between the man and the woman. Preliminary checks said the man closely knew the dead woman and hurt her with a sharp weapon.

The man ran away and went to Eppawala Hospital after the elephant hit him, and police said he also used poison. The dead woman was 45 and from Mahailluppallama, and police did not give the man's name or age but are still investigating.

Two Sri Lankan workers walking home killed by cargo protruding from truck in South Korea

cards.what_happened: Two Sri Lankan workers were killed after being struck by a cargo truck in South Korea. The accident happened while they were walking home along a road without pavement after finishing work at a nearby factory.
details: Two Sri Lankan workers in their 30s were killed in a road accident in Hwaseong, Gyeonggi Province, South Korea. They were walking home after finishing work at a nearby factory when a cargo truck's protruding roof struck them.

The accident occurred at around 9.10 p.m. on November 26 on a road with no pavement, forcing pedestrians to walk along the roadside. A section of a wooden house roof was protruding from the passing cargo truck when it hit the workers, killing them both.

The truck driver told police he had failed to properly observe the road ahead. Investigations revealed he was not under the influence of alcohol or drugs at the time of the accident, and South Korean police have taken legal action against him while investigating whether cargo-loading regulations were violated. The identities of the deceased Sri Lankans have not yet been publicly disclosed.
key_facts: Two Sri Lankan workers killed in South Korea
Accident occurred at 9.10 p.m. on November 26 in Hwaseong
Workers were walking home from a factory after their shift
A wooden house roof protruding from a cargo truck struck them
Road had no pavement, forcing pedestrians on roadside
Driver failed to observe road, not under influence of alcohol/drugs
Police took legal action and are investigating cargo-loading rules
Identities of victims not yet publicly disclosed
cards.blurb: Two Sri Lankan workers died after a cargo truck's protruding roof struck them on a road with no pavement in South Korea.
cards.spoken: A tragic accident in South Korea took the lives of two Sri Lankan workers walking home after their shift. The men, in their thirties, were struck by a cargo truck whose roof was protruding onto a road with no pavement in Hwaseong, Gyeonggi Province. The crash happened just before nine ten at night on November twenty-sixth. Police say the driver failed to see them ahead and was not under the influence of alcohol or drugs. Authorities have taken legal action and are now investigating whether cargo-loading regulations were violated. The workers' identities have not been publicly released, and investigations into the cause continue.
